svg.aria-label: Figure 1.1: Regional and Trade Geography Map of Southern Mesopotamia showing the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, Anatolian snowmelt highlands, dry-farming rainfall limit, Sumerian cities, soil salt shift north toward Babylon, and long-distance trade routes for cedar, lapis lazuli, copper, and exported woven wool.
svg.text: Figure 1.1: Southern Mesopotamia — Rivers, Rainfall Limits, and Trade Routes
Why Sumer needed irrigation canals to grow grain, and long-distance wool exports to import timber, copper, and stone

g.text: Violent spring floods hit in April–May
Rising soil salt pushed power to Babylon
